system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Project Kestrel.** The proposals below are buyer-side negotiating positions, not agreed terms. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been supplied; factual conclusions remain subject to verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery for general warranty breaches, with separate treatment for protected categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security; do not extend this cap to title, tax, specific indemnities or fraud — 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; protected categories excluded. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated — the proposed thresholds could eliminate recovery for recurring smaller breaches. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, longer category-specific periods, and preservation of properly notified claims. | **Counter at 24 months**, with reasonable notice requirements and no premature proceedings deadline — Buyer needs sufficient post-Completion reporting cycles to identify latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Standalone fundamental warranties, **100% of price cap**, no de minimis/basket, and a substantially longer claim period. | **Reject equal treatment; propose AUD 24m cap and seven-year notification period**, with survival mechanics checked under NSW law — ownership and authority are core deal risks, not ordinary business warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is stated. | Express protection for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, including appropriate attribution to Seller. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions**, preserving non-excludable rights — Seller must not obtain contractual protection for its fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; a frozen, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket disclosure; require specific, sufficiently detailed disclosures against identified warranties and preserve agreed indemnities** — document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters Buyer or advisers knew, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without deemed or adviser knowledge. | **Reject constructive knowledge and adviser imputation; exclude protected categories from any fallback** — a broad discoverability test would undermine warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although final consent and satisfaction of associated conditions are absent. | A Buyer-benefit condition requiring effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, with no unacceptable conditions or adverse contract changes. | **Require satisfactory consent and evidence that its conditions are fulfilled before Completion; only Buyer may waive** — a contract generating approximately 30% of revenue cannot be protected by a consent letter alone. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Completion repayment and effective release of all relevant security, supported by binding lender payout/release arrangements. | **Use a lender-confirmed payout and simultaneous release mechanism, with direct payment through funds flow and no double counting** — Buyer must receive the agreed debt-free business without residual lender enforcement risk. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | Conditional Completion bonuses of **AUD 420,000** treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economically bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Verify triggers and on-costs; expressly deduct or fund these amounts at Completion, with an indemnity for any shortfall** — allocation to Seller is ineffective unless reflected in payment mechanics without double counting. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified. | Evidence of cleared payment and effective ownership of all relevant materials; protection for title defects and resulting third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require payment verification and an effective confirmatory assignment before Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice** — paying a fee alone may not resolve ownership defects or consequential exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification duties remain unresolved. | Prompt independent investigation, evidence preservation, lawful containment/notification and specific allocation of pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation and remediation milestones, a specific indemnity and proportionate escrow if exposure remains unresolved** — uncertainty warrants protection, but does not establish a confirmed breach or quantify loss. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Review their combined timing, scope, necessity, termination rights and accounting treatment before accepting that characterisation. | **Assess the renewals together; restrict unapproved commitments and allocate costs under agreed debt/working-capital rules** — related commitments cannot be dismissed individually, but are not automatically debt-like liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Broad limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations and fraud. | **Insert express carve-outs, definitions and an overriding priority provision across clauses 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5** — a negotiated protection can otherwise be neutralised by a general limitation elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Verification of the entire issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options and other rights, plus effective transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with supporting corporate records, certificates and relevant searches; require clean-title warranties and releases** — the register is important evidence, not complete verification of unencumbered ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties considered settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity and tailored tax limitation period; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Reopen both: propose seven-year tax protection with appropriate extensions, and risk-calibrated IP warranties/indemnities outside unsuitable general limits** — tax liabilities and defects in a technology business’s core assets require tailored protection. |

**Priority:** Do not accept the Seller’s “settled” or “addressed” labels. Resolve Bluefen, Riverlark, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership in the Completion mechanics, while expressly preserving separate liability regimes.
=== END ADVICE ===
